<reason>A established a coherent protective gap: intelligence can identify a dangerous situation without supplying grounds to search particular individuals. B repeatedly conflated those thresholds rather than defeating the distinction. A also answered the evaluation question with an explicit stopping rule and acknowledged uncertainty. B's strongest objection—trust damage occurring before review—remained relevant, but its claims of inevitable cooperation collapse and endless deployment were overstated. A's closing more effectively weighed both irreversible harms and explained how advance limits constrain the proposed exception. The benefits remained mechanistic rather than demonstrated, limiting the margin.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>A's distinction between operation-level evidence and individualized suspicion decisively answered B's “existing powers with paperwork” objection. B subsequently acknowledged the absence of existing authority for suspicionless searches, yet continued calling expansion redundant. A's central argument therefore survived B's principal attack.</best_rebuttal>
